question.prompt: Jones covered a distance of \(50\) miles on his first trip. On a later trip he traveled \(300\) miles while going three times as fast. His new time compared with the old time was:

solutions.explanation:
Travel time equals distance divided by speed. The new distance is \(300/50=6\) times the old distance, which would require six times the time at the old speed. Traveling three times as fast divides that time by three, so
\[
\frac{\text{new time}}{\text{old time}}=\frac{6}{3}=2.
\]
The new time was twice as much, choice B.
solutions.title: Compare the distance and speed factors
